title: Bram and the Salt
premise: When the border wards of Thornfell collapse and the stars vanish, bone-carver Cyrus Thackeray discovers the dead are being silenced by a usurper who wears a drowned king's crown — and the crown is slowly wearing the king. Guided by the salt-preserved voice of his dead sister and the last loyal knight of the old dynasty, Cyrus smuggles a broken king across the mountains to the free cities, trading his own hearing of the dead piece by piece to buy passage. At the Salt Throne, Cyrus severs the crown from the king with his carving knives and the king's own confession, restoring the stars but losing his sister's voice forever; he ends the story not as a smuggler or a hero, but as the keeper of the mountain roads, finally belonging to something.
about_author: August Coldharbour is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write about borders, bones, and the people who live in the gaps between laws.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Cyrus, in his workshop above the smuggler's inn at Grayhollow, carves a memorial bone and hears the dead fall silent mid-whisper. He steps outside to a starless sky and the border wards crumbling like sugar. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: dread and disorientation — the world's oldest constants failing at once.

chapters.title: Salt in the Grain
chapters.summary: Cyrus discovers his sister Maren's voice, long dead, preserved in a salt block he inherited — the only dead voice still speaking. She warns him the wards didn't fall; they were eaten. Riders arrive asking about a fugitive on the Thornfell road. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief rekindled, first taste of conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Fugitive in the Pass
chapters.summary: Cyrus finds a wounded man in the high pass — King Aldric, alive, unmarked, half-mad, insisting he is already dead. The usurper's hunters close in. Cyrus, against every instinct for survival, takes the road only he knows. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Crown Wants
chapters.summary: Through Aldric's fevered rambling and Maren's fragments, Cyrus learns the crown is a parasite — a thing called the Hollow Regent that devours kings and now devours the wards themselves. POV: alternating Cyrus and Aldric's broken testimony. Emotional beat: horror reframing the whole war as a feeding.

chapters.title: The Knight of the Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Ser Ottoline Vane, last knight of the old dynasty, intercepts them at a flooded chapel, sword drawn, convinced Cyrus is a kidnapper. The dead in the chapel walls vouch for him — the first proof Ottoline has heard in years. POV: Ottoline. Emotional beat: a loyalist's faith, long starved, given a reason to live.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: The trio reaches the free city of Vessamy, where Cyrus bargains with the Ferryman's Guild for passage and shelter. The price: a piece of his hearing of the dead, cut away with his own carving knife. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the cost of belonging made literal and immediate.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Do Not Kneel
chapters.summary: The city council debates whether to shelter a king at all — justice here is contractual, not loyal. Ottoline's plea fails; Maren's voice, played through Cyrus's carvings, succeeds where oaths could not. POV: Ottoline. Emotional beat: cynicism cracked by something the free cities thought they'd abandoned.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Herald
chapters.summary: The Hollow Regent's herald arrives in Vessamy offering amnesty and demanding the king. The herald wears the faces of honored dead, and Cyrus recognizes Maren's face among them — a lie, but a cruel one. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: violation; grief weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Fleeing east, Cyrus leads them through a pass that only opens for those the dead forgive. Aldric, lucid for the first time, confesses his complicity in the crown's rise. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: shame as a form of courage — a king learning to be a man.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage, Again
chapters.summary: The Guild demands a second payment to move them past the blockaded coast. Cyrus pays with more of his hearing; Maren's voice grows fainter with each transaction. Ottoline confronts him about what he's spending. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: love measured against self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Bone Orchard
chapters.summary: They cross a valley where the Regent has hung the silenced dead like fruit. Aldric touches one and hears nothing — proof the silencing is total. Ottoline vows justice outside any court. POV: Ottoline. Emotional beat: grief hardened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Road
chapters.summary: A Guild guide sells their route to the Regent's armies. Ambush at the Salt Steps; Cyrus's knowledge of the roads is the only thing that saves them, but Aldric is captured's edge — wounded, recaptured, lost? No: Aldric holds, barely. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institutions he trusted to be neutral.

chapters.title: What Maren Never Said
chapters.summary: Trapped in a cave, Cyrus finally asks Maren's fading voice how she died. The answer: she died carrying a warning about the crown that Cyrus, younger and angrier, refused to hear. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the guilt beneath his grief, finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: The King Who Would Be Unmade
chapters.summary: Aldric, feverish, begs them to leave him — the crown can find him through his blood. Ottoline refuses; Cyrus proposes the heretical plan: not to hide the king, but to reach the Salt Throne and cut the crown off at its root. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: from despair to a terrible shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Army at the Border of the Map
chapters.summary: From a ridge, they watch the Regent's armies massing against the free cities — the war Cyrus's detours bought time against, now arriving. The Guild, humiliated by the traitor, offers Cyrus everything he's paid back if he surrenders the king. POV: Ottoline. Emotional beat: temptation of the easy exit, refused.

chapters.title: The Last Road In
chapters.summary: Cyrus takes them down the smugglers' road into the capital itself — the one road no army watches because no map admits it exists. Maren's voice guides the final turns and goes quiet at the threshold. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the last payment made; grief and gratitude indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Salt Throne
chapters.summary: In the throne hall, the Regent wears Aldric's face and the crown wears the Regent. Cyrus begins the severing: carving the binding-sigils from the crown's inner band while Ottoline holds the hall against the herald's dead. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the craftsman's calm inside catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Confession of Aldric Thorne
chapters.summary: The crown cannot be cut by steel alone; it needs a king's true confession as the cutting word. Aldric, lucid, names every compromise that let the thing in — and the crown cracks. The Regent unravels into salt. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: confession as the only weapon that works; justice without a trial.

chapters.title: Stars, Returning
chapters.summary: The wards reknit; the stars come back one constellation at a time while the city holds its breath. The dead's voices return to the world — all but Maren's, spent. Cyrus listens to silence for the first time since childhood. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: victory inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Weighs Its King
chapters.summary: The free cities and the old lords convene — not a coronation but an accounting. Aldric refuses the throne until his confession is read aloud and accepted. Ottoline is offered command of a new order that answers to no crown. POV: Ottoline. Emotional beat: justice as process, not restoration.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Roads
chapters.summary: Aldric offers Cyrus any reward. Cyrus asks instead for the mountain roads — made legal, mapped, and kept, so no fugitive ever needs a smuggler's mercy again. He carves a new memorial bone, blank, and leaves it so. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Salt and Starlight
chapters.summary: Epilogue: a year on, Cyrus keeps the passes, teaching travelers to read the wards. On the first anniversary of the stars' return, he sets Maren's salt block into a cairn at the pass's summit and walks home under a full sky. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into keeping — an ending that is also a beginning.
